title: Field signal diary: deployment follies & quick wins
content:
Purpose:
A compressed field-note style update covering what the private deploys team observed during the Nov 6–12 install window. Intended for eng-private-deployments standup and solutions-eng handoff. Includes triage summaries, repeated failure patterns, quick mitigations we validated, and owners for follow-up work.

High-level summary:
- Overall flux: 7 customer installs in-flight, 3 active escalations (LumenHealth, ArdentRetail, NebulaEdge).
- Recurring classes of failure: network MTU/fragmentation at customer edge, outdated firmware (HBA/BIOS) on onprem nodes, and one reproducible telemetry gap on kernel 6.x hosts that hides swap/oom signs.
- Quick wins landed: small runbook patch to preflight MTU checks + patch to node-provisioning script to fail-fast on HBA firmware below v3.2.

Incidents & notes (chronological):
1) LumenHealth — intermittent inference timeouts (customer-facing)
- Symptom: periodic 500s from model-serving process every ~40–90 minutes, coincident with a spike in packet reassembly counters on the customer firewall.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): MTU mismatch between customer edge and our load balancer leading to IP fragmentation and TCP retransmit storms when model responses exceed ~5KB.
- What we tried: enabled MSS clamping on the LB layer, pushed a lower MTU suggestion to customer CPE, and rolled a temporary model-response-size cap (truncate debug logs, batch size floor).
- Outcome: errors reduced from ~12/hr to ~1–2/hr; customer agreed to long-term MTU alignment.
- Actions: add an automated MTU probe into preflight (owner: Marcus Chen, due 2026-11-19) — see JIRA-DF-7782.

2) ArdentRetail — failed node provisioning during day-0 onprem install
- Symptom: node stayed in provisioning state; drac/firmware checks timed out; disk init hung on HP servers with HBA v2.x.
- Root cause: vendor firmware (HBA) version incompatible with RAID utility used in our node provisioning image.
- What we tried: fallback to software RAID, but performance regression unacceptable for initial validation.
- Outcome: on-site infra team rolled HBA firmware to v3.2 and provisioning completed.
- Actions: update provisioning scripts to detect HBA firmware and surface a clear remediation in UI (owner: Priya Nair, due 2026-11-24). Add vendor firmware check to docs (owner: Elena Martinez, due 2026-11-20).

3) NebulaEdge — telemetry blind spot (kernel 6.x hosts)
- Symptom: SRE observed no swap pressure metrics in our telemetry pipelines for 2 hosts running kernel 6.1. Standard sysstat and proc parsing returned empty values intermittently.
- Root cause: subtle change in procfs layout for the kernel series used by customer's distro; our parsing library (proc-parser v0.9) returns null instead of 0.
- What we tried: hotfix in telemetry agent to coerce null->0 for affected counters, and deployed to the two hosts.
- Outcome: metrics restored; we still lack historical coverage for the window.
- Actions: upgrade proc-parser and add unit tests with kernel-6.x proc samples (owner: Omar Haddad, due 2026-11-30).

Observations & patterns (non-incident):
- Many field teams still rely on verbal checks for MTU and leave jumbo frames enabled by default — we should document the recommended MTU policy and provide a one-liner check.
- A surprising number of customers have older vendor images for BMC management; build-time checks for IPMI/DRAC responsiveness reduce wasted drive swaps.
- DNS timeouts in one customer (edge DNS load balancing) correlated with model-serving spikes during bulk embeds; caching TTLs on the LB helped.

Runbook / process suggestions (short list):
- Preflight extension: add MTU probe + BMC firmware probe + HBA fingerprint check. Keep it fast (<90s). (owner: Marcus Chen)
- Provisioning UX: when HBA mismatch detected, present explicit remediation ("update firmware to >=3.2" and provide vendor link). (owner: Priya Nair)
- Telemetry contract: define minimal metric set we must never lose (swap, mem_free, load1, load5, disk_io) and add integration tests for common kernels. (owner: Omar Haddad)

Decisions from weekly standup (2026-11-12):
- Agree to add the MTU probe to preflight as an MVP. No new infra required; reuses existing LB health-check path. (Marcus)
- Defer large-scale node image rebuild until next sprint; patch scripts + UX are sufficient for short term. (Priya)
- Create a "kernel-compat" test harness and schedule an infra-qa block next week. (Omar)

Action items (short):
- Marcus Chen: implement MTU preflight probe + automated remediation note (due 2026-11-19).
- Priya Nair: add HBA firmware detection to provisioning scripts + UX copy (due 2026-11-24).
- Omar Haddad: upgrade proc-parser, add kernel-6.x unit tests, and schedule a QA run (due 2026-11-30).
- Elena Martinez: draft customer-facing note summarizing MTU and firmware pitfalls; coordinate with solutions-eng to include in customer onboarding guide (due 2026-11-20).

Known risks / blockers for next week:
- If any major account refuses firmware updates (regulatory/policy), we will need to accept a longer provisioning path or provide a sworn compatibility waiver — legal/solutions-eng involvement likely.
- Telemetry upgrade touches agents; if packaging delays exceed 1 sprint, visibility on new installs will be reduced.

Requests for help / asks:
- Solutions-eng: prepare a short vendor-firmware troubleshooting cheat-sheet we can attach to the onboarding playbook.
- SRE: if you have an existing MTU probe we can borrow, flag it in Slack #sre-runbooks.

Appendix (quick debug notes and commands used):
- MTU probe (one-liner we tested): ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1500; ping -M do -s 1400 <customer-gw> -c 3
- HBA detect (script snippet): smartctl --scan | grep -i hba || echo "no-hba-detected"
- Telemetry patch: proc-parser v0.9 -> v1.1 (coerceNullCounters flag)

Concluding note:
This week felt like a mix of classic infra hygiene issues and a couple of interesting edge-cases caused by evolving kernels and customer networking. The quick runbook patches reduced pain substantially; focus next week is about converting those quick fixes into automated preflight checks and making the failure modes transparent in provisioning UX so site teams (and customers) can resolve without escalation.

Meeting attendees (standup 2026-11-12): Elena Martinez, Marcus Chen, Priya Nair, Omar Haddad, Lina Ghosh (solutions-eng), Tom Brooks (sre).
